correctness.rationale: The endpoint quotient is correctly derived, but the final claimed absolute Floquet multiplier μ=Δ1Δ2 L2 Fcorrect is false with L2 **exactly as defined in source Theorem 3.5**. From the actual P,Q, the residual needed after subtracting P/x and Q/y is R=P_x−P/x+Q_y−Q/y; direct differentiation yields R_P=rx/K−r a x/K²−2rx²/K²+h0 g(y)² xy/(1+h0 g(y)x)² and R_Q=s y b1/(y+b1)²−s a1 y/(x+c1), g(y)=p0+a0 y/(1+b0 y). The printed L2 has rx/K−2rx²/K²+h0 g(y)xy/(1+h0g(y)x)² and s y b1/(y+b1)²−a1/(x+c1): three nonzero omissions. Their residual difference is −r a x/K²+h0(g²−g)xy/(1+h0gx)²+a1(1−s y)/(x+c1). At article sample positive values (r=.85,K=100,a=4,p0=.26,a0=1,b0=2,h0=5,s=.25,b1=1,c1=4,a1=1,x=30,y=40), the P and Q residual differences are approximately −0.09576364 and −0.26470588, respectively. Replacing the endpoint factor alone does not turn printed L2 into exp∫R. Original advertised full multiplier formula is not proved and is generally false. Agreement locus for the isolated endpoint factors is still valid; a genuine corrected full Floquet formula requires replacing L2 as well.
